fields.meta_title: Student Registration Form Builder for Schools | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a student registration form that sets each child's grade, collects the records you keep and saves every student to a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Student Registration Form That Places Each Student
fields.hero_description: Describe how your school places students. Emergent builds the student registration form and files each new student, with their documents, in your own database.
fields.features_heading: What Gets Settled Before the First Day
fields.features_subheading: Registration is where a student's grade and paperwork get settled. These are the parts a school office stops doing by hand.
fields.feature_1:
Grade placement from the birth date

Enter your cutoff date and the age for each grade. The form reads the child's birth date, suggests a grade and flags anyone who falls a few days on the wrong side of the line.
fields.feature_2:
Document uploads on the student's row

Ask for a birth certificate and last year's report card as uploads. Each file is saved next to the student's answers, and a missing one keeps the registration marked incomplete.
fields.feature_3:
A placement check inside the form

Add a short quiz as the last step of registration. The score is calculated on submit and decides the student's group, and the teacher sees every answer before the first class.
fields.feature_4:
Brothers and sisters in one sitting

Parents add each child in turn and type the address and guardians only once. Every sibling gets a separate record with a shared family link that admissions uses for priority.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders for anything still missing

Choose who hears about gaps and when. A family with no immunization record gets an email after 5 days, and the registrar sees a list of students who are not yet complete.
fields.feature_6:
The code goes to your repository

Export the whole app to GitHub when your developer wants to connect it to a student information system. It can also run on your school's own domain instead of a shared form link.

fields.tab_content_1:
Birthdays past September 1 wait on a readiness visit

Corbin Hill School places every new student by birth date. A child must turn 5 by September 1 to start kindergarten. Theo Lang's parents apply for kindergarten with a September 14 birthday, and the form flags him instead of placing him. Admissions books a readiness visit, and his grade is set after it.
fields.tab_content_2:
Twelve correct or fewer places a student in Foundations

Northside Learning Lab tutors middle school math. Its registration ends with a 20-question placement check. Students with 12 or fewer right join Foundations on Tuesdays, and 13 and up join Bridge on Thursdays. Each group seats 8. Tutors open the scores the night before the first session.
fields.tab_content_3:
Eleven sibling seats, then 37 drawn by lottery

Juniper Montessori had 140 applications for 48 kindergarten seats this year. Siblings of enrolled students were placed first and took 11 seats, leaving 37 for a random draw on March 3. The 92 families left over were numbered on a waitlist in the order they were drawn.
fields.tab_content_4:
Transfer records requested by email on submit

A family that moves in February registers a new student at Riverton Charter. The form asks for the previous school and its records office email. When the parent submits, the app emails that office a records request and marks the student Records requested. After 10 days with no file, the registrar gets a reminder.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Student Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Settle the placement rules and the paperwork first. The prompt is the last step, not the first.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down the grades you enroll
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the rule for a full grade
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the grades or groups you take and the rule that puts a student in each one. A birth date cutoff suits kindergarten, while tutoring groups are better sorted by a placement score. Note how many seats each grade or group holds.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down every file your office keeps for a new student, such as a birth certificate or an immunization record. Mark each upload as required or optional. Records that come straight from a previous school, like a transcript, belong in a request step instead of an upload.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick the order for a full grade before applications open. Some schools seat siblings first and draw the rest at random, while others take students in the order they register. Write the rule down exactly, because the form will apply it word for word.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste your grades, documents and seat rules into the prompt. Emergent builds the form, the placement logic and a database with one row per student. Ask for changes the same way, for example adding a pre-K class or a second campus.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Put each signature where it belongs
fields.howto_step_5_des: Give the handbook acknowledgment and the photo permission their own screens, each with a signature box. A guardian who has not signed one cannot submit. The signature is saved on the student's record with the date it was given.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Name the person who follows up when an upload is missing or a previous school stays quiet. Set how many days pass before the first reminder, and send it to that person's email or Slack instead of a shared inbox nobody reads.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Register two made-up siblings, one with a birthday a few days past your cutoff. Check that the flag appears, that both children share a family link and that the uploads land on the right rows. Delete the test family before the link goes out.

plan.angle: The live top 10 splits between template pages (AidaForm, Formplus, FormAssembly, a pdfFiller copy of Broward County's form) and the paperwork itself: Pinterest printables, a school's own Jotform, Ohio's enrollment handout and a college child center's PDF. Every one of them stops at the blank form. A private school, tutoring center or small charter registering students needs the decisions that come after it: which grade a child belongs in, which group a placement score points to, who gets a seat when applications outnumber them, and whether a transfer's old records ever arrived. This page shows four programs making those decisions on the form, answers the proof-of-enrollment questions people ask from the registrar's side, and keeps every student in a database the school owns.
tab_stories: A K-8 private school places each new student by birth date against its September 1 cutoff, and a kindergarten applicant born September 14 is flagged for a readiness visit before a grade is set.
A tutoring center puts a 20-question math check inside registration, and a score of 12 or lower sends the student to the Tuesday Foundations group while 13 and up go to Thursday Bridge.
A Montessori school with 48 kindergarten seats and 140 applications gives 11 seats to siblings of enrolled students, fills the other 37 by random draw and numbers the remaining 92 on a waitlist.

A charter middle school registering a February transfer emails the previous school a records request on submit, marks the student as records requested and reminds the registrar after 10 days of silence.
